proposed_by: claude-opus-5-5 (H2 ownership and applicability reconciliation, 2026-11-09), revising ap-k5-conditional-context-boundary-h2
rationale: The replay informs H2's economics but does not support its specific levels: H2's levels rest on compaction points (lines 88-90), and the reference reuses the replay's 116K floor value (line 105). Replayed from the recorded work of gpt-6-sol builders before Sol 6.1 and the 250K limit, the replay projects (models, not measures) about 30% higher cost at every tested threshold when it assumes the observed Codex-native total restart floor of about 116K, with modelled break-even near 75K. These projections do not establish H2's threshold optimum or its current economics. The earlier flat "+35% at 70-80K" reading was corrected the same day to the rediscovery-free row (ev-20261018-m22-same-day-correction). The relation vocabulary has no 'informs', so the relation is recorded as not established.

proposed_by: claude-opus-5-5 (H2 ownership and applicability reconciliation, 2026-11-09), revising ap-k6-no-limit-context-boundary-h2
rationale: Supports placing H2's levels below automatic compaction in sessions without a configured limit, not their optimality. The band floor 235,000 sits just under the lowest automatic compaction this finding records (gpt-6-astra, 239,130 of 258,400; 10 compactions in 9 threads). Every no-limit gpt-6.1-sol compaction (437,522 to 456,118) lies far above both levels, so for those sessions H2 warns early. The trigger's 35,000 margin below the floor is chosen, not measured (probe lines 46-49), and the reference states H2 as a hypothesis, not a calibrated optimum (lines 90-91).

proposed_by: claude-opus-5-5 (H2 ownership and applicability reconciliation, 2026-11-09), revising ap-k6-limit-context-boundary-h2
rationale: Supports, at low strength, applying H2's token levels to gpt-6.1-sol sessions started under the 250K limit: the one such session that grew past 250K compacted at 248,987 (n = 1), 13,987 above the 235,000 band floor. The finding has no gpt-6-astra observation under the limit; the Astra point the levels also rest on (239,130) comes from the no-limit finding. The same finding shows sessions whose root started before the limit compacting near 449K (n = 2) or reaching 338,682 without compacting (n = 1); for them H2 warns early. The levels hold only while ~/.codex/config.toml sets this limit (lines 100-101), a mutable off-repo setting recorded as unverified.

proposed_by: claude-opus-5-5 (H2 ownership and applicability reconciliation, 2026-11-09), revising ap-k4-effort-cost-table-effort-row
rationale: Supports the row's per-call clause for Sol only: on Codex gpt-6-sol, weighted cost per call was 15.9, 16.4, 15.8 and 16.5 K at low, medium, high and xhigh effort over 35,503 October calls, because cached context re-send (about 77%) dominates. The finding has no gpt-6-astra measurement, so it does not support the row's Astra half. It measures cost per call, not total task cost; effort's effect through call count and correction rounds is unmeasured (notes lines 221-225), which the row's second clause leaves open. Current defaults use gpt-6.1-sol; whether the per-call result holds for it is not established (currency drifting).
